title: A Giant Storm Soaks New York and New Jersey — Flights, Concerts, and Games Cancelled
summary:
Imagine looking out your window and seeing your street turned into a river. That's what happened in parts of New Jersey on Saturday as a powerful storm called a nor'easter slammed the northeastern United States.

A nor'easter is a big storm that comes from the northeast. This one brought heavy rain, strong winds, and flooding to millions of people from Virginia all the way to Maine. New York and New Jersey both declared states of emergency.

In Surf City and Manasquan, New Jersey, streets and homes were underwater. More than 100,000 households lost electricity. Airports were a mess: more than 2,400 flights were delayed and nearly 1,200 were cancelled.

"I urge all New Jerseyans to take this storm seriously, stay alert and follow local guidance," Governor Mikie Sherrill said. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani told residents, "Don't travel if you don't have to. Do not drive or walk through floodwater."

Saturday's full moon made the flooding worse by pulling the ocean higher. Big events were called off too: a Red Sox game, a professional soccer match, and the Global Citizen Festival concert in Central Park. Even Ed Sheeran's concert near Boston was cancelled for safety.
why_it_matters: A big storm can change your whole week in a hurry — a cancelled game, a flooded road, or a dark house — so every family should know how to get ready and stay out of floodwater.

background_read: A nor'easter gets its name from the direction its winds come from — the northeast. These storms often form in fall and winter, when cold air from the north meets warm, wet air over the ocean.
In 2012, a huge storm called Superstorm Sandy flooded parts of New York and New Jersey, so people in those areas already know how dangerous storm flooding can be.

The Global Citizen Festival (a big free concert in New York City's Central Park that raises money to fight poverty) and the Red Sox (a professional baseball team from Boston) both had to change their plans because of this storm.
Article_Structure: WHO: Millions of people in the northeastern United States, plus New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani
WHAT: A nor'easter brought heavy rain, strong winds, and flooding; states of emergency were declared and events and flights were cancelled
WHERE: From Virginia all the way to Maine, with street flooding in New Jersey towns like Surf City and Manasquan
WHY: Streets and homes went underwater, more than 100,000 households lost power, and the full moon made the ocean higher and the flooding worse

perspectives.description: Governors and mayors acted fast, declaring states of emergency and telling people to stay home, because flooded roads are the biggest danger.
People whose flights, soccer match, baseball game, or concert were called off felt disappointed, but the cancellations were meant to keep crowds safe.
Families in towns like Surf City and Manasquan watched water fill their streets and homes, so now they face cleanup and repair costs.
